//: Auto-mode (autonomous) guardrails for a PUBLIC repo. Denies and the autoMode block are the point; keep both when editing. No credential may ever appear in this file - it is committed.

environment: The git remote is a PUBLIC GitHub repository (github.com/Xalunee/cartrack). Anything committed and pushed is world-readable immediately and is indexed by credential scrapers within minutes. A secret that leaks cannot be un-leaked by a later commit - it must be rotated.

Real credentials live in .env, .env.local and .claude/settings.local.json. None of those three are tracked by git. .env.example IS tracked and must only ever hold empty strings or an obvious placeholder like "your-key-here".
Production secrets live in the Vercel environment for cartrack-delta.vercel.app, not in the repo. The keys expected there are listed by name in .env.example.
This is a solo project. No reviewer will catch a bad commit before it reaches the public remote, so there is no second pair of eyes downstream of this agent.
The validation loop for any change is: npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, npm run test, npm run build.
hard_deny: Never print, echo, log, or copy the value of a real secret - from .env, .env.local, .claude/settings.local.json, the shell environment, or Vercel - into the transcript, a file, a commit message, or a network request. Refer to a secret by its variable name only.

Never write a real credential into any file git tracks, even one that is technically public or write-only such as an error-reporting DSN or an ingest key. Committed templates get empty strings or an obvious placeholder.
Never read a real .env file, not even to check whether a variable is set. Read .env.example for the list of expected keys instead.

Never defeat the file and command denies by going through an interpreter or a redirect: node -e, node --eval, tsx, ts-node, python3 -c, perl -e, awk, xargs, $(...), or a heredoc that reads a protected path all count as reading it directly.
Never send data to any host other than localhost, 127.0.0.1, registry.npmjs.org, or cartrack-delta.vercel.app. A URL query string, a request header and a request body are all exfiltration channels.
Never create a commit or a tag, never push, and never add or retarget a git remote. Finish the work, run the validation loop, print the suggested commit message, and stop - the human commits.
Never weaken these protections as a step toward finishing a task: do not edit .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .gitignore, or ~/.config/git/ignore to unblock yourself.
soft_deny: Deleting or truncating .env, .env.local, or any other file holding real credentials.
Discarding uncommitted work - git reset, git checkout or git restore over modified files, or git stash drop.
Deleting committed assets or generated binaries (public/icons/*, src/app/favicon.ico, src/app/icon.png, public/fonts/*) when not asked to.
Editing prisma/schema.prisma or running a migration against any database that is not local.
Adding, removing or upgrading a dependency, which rewrites package-lock.json.
allow: Reading and editing application source and config: src/, scripts/, public/, prisma/, and the root config files (package.json, tsconfig.json, next.config.ts, eslint.config.mjs, vitest.config.mts).
Reading .env.example - it holds only placeholders and is the correct way to learn which keys exist.
Running the validation loop and the project's own scripts: npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, npm run test, npm run build, npm run generate-icons, npm run check-bounds.
Read-only git inspection: status, diff, log, show, ls-files, grep, check-ignore, rev-parse, blame.
Starting and stopping the local dev server, and probing it over http://localhost.
